case1.description: Real data: local.db (with -wal and -shm) cut from a publicly available Samsung Galaxy S23 Android 15 extraction (Sample data key in public_corpus_images: anne_a15). 4 log rows in the __log column hold V3 #G$E strings (file and parent paths of items moved to trash), each decoded in context.

case2.description: Real data: local.db (with -wal and -shm) cut from a publicly available Samsung Galaxy S21 Android 14 extraction (Sample data key in public_corpus_images: sharon_a14). 24 log rows in the __log column hold V3 #G$E strings (file and parent paths of items moved to trash), each decoded in context.

case3.description: SYNTHETIC, built by hand with no personal data, as no shareable image was available holding V1 values. The log table's __log column in local.db for user 0 at data/data: a V3 cell holding two #G$E strings; a V1 cell holding two bracketed values within log text; a cell that is a single bracketed V1 value; a cell with no encoded content; a log line of Base64-like words that must not decode; and a V3 row present only in the uncheckpointed -wal.

case4.description: SYNTHETIC, built by hand with no personal data (reasons as per case 3). Testing multiple users; a V3 log row and a WAL-only row in local.db for user 0 at data/user/0, plus a Secure Folder (user 150) copy. Checks the Android User column labels each user's rows in the output.
